subject.title: Manage Claw cron jobs through the gateway

question: Should canonical `agents delete` remove scheduler jobs that this experimental Claw feature records as owned by the deleted agent, or is retaining those jobs an intentional supported lifecycle boundary?
rationale: This choice changes the durable ownership contract of the existing generic agent-deletion path and cannot be resolved safely by a Claw-specific workaround alone.

options.title: Make canonical deletion clean owned cron jobs
options.body: Extend the canonical deletion lifecycle to remove only scheduler jobs proven by durable ownership records to belong to the agent, preserving retry-safe partial-state behavior.

options.title: Keep deletion behavior unchanged
options.body: Accept that ordinary deletion can retain Claw-created schedules, document the supported removal path, and explicitly treat orphan cleanup as a separate core product commitment.

recommendation.title: Make canonical deletion clean owned cron jobs
recommendation.body: Extend the canonical deletion lifecycle to remove only scheduler jobs proven by durable ownership records to belong to the agent, preserving retry-safe partial-state behavior.
